Q: List all GitHub repos for an organization - INCLUDING those in teams A:

You can use the GitHub CLI tool for that. Specifically you need the gh repo list command.

Example

$ gh repo list {organization-name}

Note that by default this command returns maximum 30 results. To increase the maximum number of repositories to list, use the --limit flag (short variant -L) with the desired max number:

# Specifying the maximum of 100 repos to list
$ gh repo list {organization-name} -L 100

NOTE

To start using the gh command, you need to authenticate with your GitHub account first:

$ gh auth login

For more info read the official GitHub CLI manual.

Q: Formula to extract first number in cell ignoring the remainder, however number can be one or two characters and varies A:

With using REGEX the below formula in cell B91 (and dragdown) gives the following reuslt:

=REGEXEXTRACT(A91,"^\d+")

Q: Service selling platform A:

Just... start.

Starting a project is the hardest step sometimes, but if you don't start, you won't finish it.

Perhaps design the UI first, so you know how users are gonna interact with the service. Or you could start by thinking about what you need to know about every user, every booking, ..., and you could make the DB first (that's how I would start, so you know what you work with, and what might be shown to users).

How to start generally is different from person to person. Incase you have the specifications already (which I suppose you do, else I'd start with that), it's now "only" a matter of implementing your ideas in code.

Q: How can I solve Flutter web API CORS error only with Dart code? A:

Using Flutter’s Web Dev Proxy (with web_dev_config.yaml)

Flutter recently introduced a built-in web development proxy, which is really useful for avoiding CORS issues during local development.

You can configure it using a web_dev_config.yaml file at the root of your project.

server:
  host: "0.0.0.0"   # Bind to all interfaces
  port: 8000        # Dev server port

  proxy:
    - target: "http://localhost:3000"   # Backend API
      prefix: "/api/"                   # Requests starting with /api/ are proxied
    # our backend uses seperate prefix for files  
    - target: "http://localhost:3000"   # Same or different backend
      prefix: "/files/"                 # Requests starting with /files/ are proxied

Any request from your Flutter web app to:

  • /api/... → forwarded to http://localhost:3000/...

  • /files/... → forwarded to http://localhost:3000/...

final response = await http.get(Uri.parse('/api/users'));

This will automatically be proxied to:

http://localhost:3000/api/users

Optional: Enable HTTPS

https:
  cert-path: "/path/to/cert.pem"
  cert-key-path: "/path/to/key.pem"

If you’re dealing with multiple backends or microservices, you can add multiple proxy entries the same way.

Q: How to rename my bins created with dplyr mutate cut A:

Yes, you can name your bins as "1:10" instead of traditional interval labels, as long as the meaning is clear to users. Custom naming can work well for internal systems or specific workflows, but it's important to ensure there's no confusion, adding a simple legend or explanation can help users understand what each bins represents. In practical applications, especially in waste managements or storage system, you can explore a range of well-designed and costomizable disposal solutionon disposalking.com, where yo'll find options suited for both organized labelling and high-usage enviroments.
